# Preview feature status

The published development release is [0.4.0-preview.3](install.qmd). The verified
WSL user-local command also reports that version. See
[release evidence](release-delivery.qmd) for the exact source and checks.

This is an early Rust CLI for disposable analysis projects. A development preview
does not mean the complete roadmap is finished. Use independent backups and sample
data while evaluating it. The existing projr R package and thesis remain unchanged.

| Area | Available Rust behavior | Verification and limits |
|---|---|---|
| Project selection | Explicit root; nearest recognized ancestor; markerless cwd fallback; shallow default script discovery. | Cross-platform fixtures cover markers, nested invocation and explicit override. Root recognition includes Python/Julia markers; that does not imply Julia execution or a wrapper. |
| Configuration and init | Active root YAML required; legacy alias/ambiguity rule; profile precedence; explicitly declared resource directories; local-only directory initialization. | Cross-platform configuration/error-preservation fixtures. Old no-config roadmap assumptions were superseded. |
| Execution context | Ordered explicit scripts/hooks; native cwd with explicit project-root override; supported Quarto/R Markdown root controls; unsafe/unknown layouts fail early. | Real Python/R/rendering acceptance and cross-platform fixtures passed. Direct R API/IDE parity remains unproved. |
| Automation | Opt-in protocol-v1 JSON, capability version, typed queries, noninteractive command worker, nonzero failures; child logs on stderr. | Cross-platform machine tests. Static coarse error codes; no invented attempt/release record on success. |
| Preview preservation | The released CLI restores captured managed state after successful/failed previews. Cache results remain. | Included through the reviewed recovery dependency; final integrated tests and actual released-binary checks passed. Generated-output path queries use the safe cache by default; arbitrary writes are not isolated. |
| Production safety groundwork | Path guards, bounded local failure recovery, optional checked Git publication and verified CAS bytes. | Focused fixtures and reviews; incomplete release identity/provenance/retry model. This page is not an invitation to run on valuable production data. |
| Ordinary remotes | Local/GitHub latest/archive publication and guarded single-label restore; file/manifest/none inspection, four strategies and both supported cues. | Full mocked CLI matrix; bounded real latest/archive round-trip. Complete option parity and M2 remain unfinished. |
| Binary delivery | [Development prerelease 0.4.0-preview.3](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.4.0-preview.3) supplies versioned Linux/Windows x86-64 assets with mandatory checksums. | Exact-tag workflow, uploaded/public asset hashes and both native binary smokes passed. WSL user-local installation and tiny success/failure Python previews passed. Other platforms are not supplied. |

Still unfinished: direct projr/quarto R API/RStudio parity, existing R helper
integration, automatic isolation of every script write,
durable attempt/release identifiers, complete input/code/config/dependency provenance,
multi-writer/crash atomicity and analysis-free publication retry. Capture/recovery
cannot undo arbitrary external script effects or guarantee concurrent readers never
observe temporary changes. User/third-party logs are not automatically secret-redacted.

M1 is delivered as the useful local CLI preview in 0.4.0-preview.2. It requires
active root configuration; initialization is optional. Explicit file-based
R/Python/report steps, captured context, inspectable cached results and honest
structured failures work without Git credentials. Supported previews preserve
recorded final/archive/version state on success and failure. Runtime path guards
and preflight remain essential; arbitrary child code is not sandboxed.

General command/argv forms, stronger process confinement and broader maintenance
audits remain follow-ups. M2 records/provenance/retry and later frontend work
are not completed by M1.
See [delivery boundaries](release-delivery.qmd), [behavior](behavior.qmd) and the
[compatibility log](compatibility.qmd) for supported details and remaining gaps.
